meta.caution: Per-part masses of 2026 F1 cars are not published. Only the PU mass groups, the driver + ballast floor and the Minimum Mass are fixed by regulation. Never quote a best value as measured.

minimum_mass.car_mass_definition: car incl. tyres + Mass of the Driver + Driver Ballast, without fuel
minimum_mass.heat_hazard: C4.6: +5 kg in a Heat Hazard TTCS (driver cooling ≥ 5 kg); +2 kg otherwise at such a competition

nominal_tyre_mass.basis: Published by Pirelli (mean of 50 tyres per axle after the last pre-season test); the published figure was not found in any public source. 44 kg = the FIA/F1/Pirelli 768 kg headline minus the 724 kg base in Issue 8 (2024), the same assumption RaceFans footnotes. 46 kg would make the minima 770 / 772 kg, which matches team spec sheets quoting 770 kg (Haas 'minimum', Ferrari) and McLaren's 772 kg, but those may be quali or actual figures.

driver.note: the seat and driving equipment are INSIDE the Mass of the Driver; the harness is not

options.option: a: MGU-K speed ratio in RV-PU-ERS

power_unit.note: Drawing 9 (for reference): 'Min ICE+TC+Powerbox 130kg', ESME 35, MGU-K 16 + assumed 4 kg transmission, total 185 kg. The TC is inside the ICE group, and ICE + MGU-K = 150 kg in every option.

consistency.method: Bottom-up: every component above. Top-down: reported 2026 cars sit at the 768 kg race minimum ±(under to +26 kg) with their parts alone (RN365-WEIGHTS, PLANETF1-WILLIAMS, MCLAREN-SPEC), so a car 'on the limit' has parts summing to ≈ 768 kg. The bottom-up sum falls short by the mass public part figures never capture (inserts, fixings, local reinforcement, fluids, brackets). Reconciliation: regulation, official, reported and geometry-derived components are held fixed; every component marked scaled_by_reconciliation is multiplied by one factor k so the parts reach the target.
